title: AmgT: Algebraic Multigrid Solver on Tensor Cores
problem: Existing AMG solver implementations on GPUs have not exploited tensor core units and their low precision compute capabilities for sparse matrix operations. SpGEMM and SpMV kernels in AMG consume significant compute time but cannot efficiently utilize tensor cores with current data formats.
motivation: Tensor cores offer order-of-magnitude speedups for matrix operations; exploiting them in AMG could dramatically accelerate sparse linear system solvers across HPC applications.
method: AmgT creates a unified way to store sparse matrices (matrices with mostly zeros) that enables specialized GPU units called tensor cores to speed up both the setup phase (matrix multiplication, or SpGEMM) and the solve phase (matrix-vector multiplication, or SpMV) of algebraic multigrid solving. The design uses mixed precision—storing some numbers at lower precision—to reduce memory bandwidth and overhead from converting between storage formats. The implementation is integrated into the HYPRE library, so existing software can use it without changes.
key_novelty: The first unified sparse matrix storage format enabling tensor cores to accelerate both SpGEMM (sparse matrix multiplication for setup) and SpMV (matrix-vector multiplication for solving) in algebraic multigrid, with mixed precision support.
contributions: Unified sparse storage format optimized for tensor core execution
Mixed precision AMG algorithm implementation reducing memory traffic
HYPRE library integration enabling production adoption
Demonstrated 1.46× to 2.24× geomean speedups across A100, H100, and MI210 GPUs
primary_theme: Tensor core acceleration for sparse matrix operations in AMG
